question: Would egg-nature apply to each principle even without the term mass of reality?
premises: One might think each principle could be an egg even without the term mass of reality.
This would imply egg-nature in the principles individually.
The verse raises a challenge to that consequence.
inference: The text questions whether egg-nature can rightly be assigned to each principle on its own.
uncertainties: The verse is transitional and its force is partly completed by the next verse.
plain_english: Someone might think that, even without using the term 'mass of reality', each principle by itself could have the nature of an egg; but the text challenges that idea.
